draft.title: The World Health Organization
card: The World Health Organization (WHO) is an agency of the United Nations. It works to coordinate health action between countries, so that they can act together on problems that cross borders.
The WHO sets standards and guidelines, such as advice on safe levels of pollutants in drinking water. Countries may use this advice when they make their own health policies.
The WHO tracks disease outbreaks around the world. It collects reports from countries and warns others, so that a disease can be spotted and slowed early.
The WHO also leads and supports campaigns, such as vaccination programs to reduce diseases like polio and measles. It works with governments, and it does not run a country's health system.
draft.remember: The WHO coordinates countries, sets standards, tracks outbreaks and backs campaigns.

a.q: Which of these is an example of the WHO tracking disease outbreaks?
opts: Collecting reports of a new virus from many countries
Building a public hospital in a country with few clinics
Paying the doctor bills of people who are sick abroad
Making laws that every country must follow on health
a.why: Tracking means gathering reports from countries and warning others so a disease can be slowed early. The WHO does not build hospitals or pay bills, and its guidelines are advice that countries may use, not laws.
a.clue: Tracking is about gathering information and sharing warnings.

b.q: Several countries in one region report cases of the same new illness. Which action fits the WHO's role?
opts: Sharing the reports and advising all countries on a response
Taking over the health systems of the affected countries
Treating each sick person in the region at its own clinics
Waiting until one country asks for a law to be passed
b.why: The WHO coordinates countries by sharing outbreak information and giving advice. It works with governments and does not run their health systems, so taking over is wrong. Treating every patient directly is also not its main role.
b.clue: The WHO works with governments, not in place of them.

a.best: Collecting reports of a new virus from many countries

b.best: Sharing the reports and advising all countries on a response
